info.title: Eye Diagnosis Web API
info.description: Python rewrite of the non-Agent domains. Contract notes live in docs/migration-decisions.md.

post.description:
``UserServiceImpl#userLogin``.

The validation order and the Chinese messages are copied exactly, because
the frontend surfaces ``msg`` verbatim in a toast:

``PARAMS_IS_NULL`` -> ``ACCOUNT_ERROR`` -> ``PASSWORD_ERROR`` ->
``FAIL_LOGIN``.

``FAIL_LOGIN`` is deliberately used for both "no such account" and "wrong
password", so the response cannot be used to enumerate accounts.

The lookup is restricted to ``is_delete = 0`` because MyBatis Plus appends
that predicate automatically for a ``@TableLogic`` field, so a
logically-deleted account cannot log in under Java either.

``UserServiceImpl#userLogout``.

Not idempotent, on purpose: logging out without a session is an error in
Java (``NOT_LOGIN_ERROR`` + ``NO_LOGIN``) and some frontend flow depends on
being told the difference between "you were signed in" and "you were not".
Making it idempotent would be a compatible-but-different contract, so the
Java behaviour is kept until a ticket says otherwise.

The caller is taken as a dependency rather than by calling
``get_login_user(request)`` inline: the latter leaves its own ``db``
parameter unresolved, which fails the row lookup and reports 500 -- "you
could not log out" -- to every user who *was* signed in.

get.description:
``UserServiceImpl#getLoginUser`` + ``getLoginUserVO``.

Anonymous -> ``NOT_LOGIN_ERROR``, same as Java. The frontend's
``stores/user.ts`` treats "not 0, or no data" as signed out and its router
guard redirects to the login page, so the behaviour is unchanged.

post.description:
``UserServiceImpl#userRegister``.

Validation order is copied exactly; each branch throws a different Chinese
message and the frontend surfaces it verbatim.

``UserController#userAdd``.

The controller requires an explicit initial password rather than falling
back to a default (``UserController.java:115-118``), and writes the
BCrypt hash separately from the bean copy.

get.description:
Deviation: Java returns the entity *with* ``userPassword``. Unused by
the frontend and leaky, so the desensitized view is returned instead.

post.description:
``UserController#updateUser``.

``updateTime`` is set explicitly: in Java it relies on the column's
``ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP``, which SQLAlchemy does not trigger for a
plain ORM UPDATE.

post.summary: 获取分页用户列表（缓存版本）
post.description:
Redis-cached variant, mirroring ``listUserVOByPageWithCache``.

The key is an MD5 of the request body, as in Java, and the TTL is
``300 + random(0, 300)`` seconds to spread expirations.

Logical delete.

``removeById`` on a ``@TableLogic`` field issues ``UPDATE t_user SET
isDelete=1`` rather than a DELETE, so the row stays for the Agent tables'
foreign keys while disappearing from every query.

``UserServiceImpl#updateOwnProfile`` -- always targets the session user.

Java is queried on every subsequent request, including after profile edits.

``UserServiceImpl#uploadUserAvatar``.

Multipart field is ``file`` (singular). The COS prefix is
``public/{userId}``, matching ``String.format("public/%s", loginUser.getId())``.

``UserServiceImpl#reexamineDiagnosis``.

Ownership is enforced: a user may only flag their own diagnosis, otherwise
``NO_AUTH_ERROR``.

``DiagnosisServiceImpl.uploadDiagnosisPicture`` (:90-113).

The ``id`` form field is accepted and **ignored** -- Java's
``saveOrUpdate`` inserts because the freshly built entity has no id, so the
DTO's id never reaches the database even though the frontend sends it.

``username`` is ``None`` here even though the row has an owner: Java calls
``DiagnosisManageVO.objToVo(diagnosis)`` directly (:112), not
``getDiagnosisManageVO``, so this one endpoint skips the ``t_user`` lookup
that the list endpoints perform.

``listDiagnosisVOByPage``.

The three list endpoints differ only in caching. ``userId`` is overwritten
with the session user, so a client posting another user's id gets their own
rows back rather than someone else's.

post.summary: 获取分页诊断列表（缓存版本）
post.description:
``listDiagnosisVOByPageWithCache`` (:68-110).

The key is ``md5(userId:userRole:json(dto))``, so a shared cache can never
serve one user's medical records to another. The ``json(dto)`` term is not
byte-identical to Hutool's, so a cache entry written by Java is simply a
miss here -- harmless, and only possible before Nginx finishes the cutover.

``listMyDiagnosisVOByPage`` (:113-131) -- identical to ``/list/page/vo``.

The Java source looks like it calls a *static* setter
(``DiagnosisQueryDTO.setUserId(...)`` with the class name), which would not
compile. It does, because the parameter is declared
``DiagnosisQueryDTO DiagnosisQueryDTO`` -- the variable name shadows the
type name (JLS 6.5.2), so it is an ordinary instance call and this endpoint
is scoped to the caller exactly like the other two.

Logical delete -- ``removeById`` on a ``@TableLogic`` field issues
``UPDATE t_diagnosis SET isDelete=1``, keeping the row for referential
integrity while hiding it from every query. Returns ``false`` for a row
that is absent or already deleted, as Java does.

``DiagnosisServiceImpl.doDiagnosis`` (:169-252), with the gRPC hop
replaced by :meth:`web.inference.InferenceEngine.diagnose`.

Failure mode differs from Java's and that is the point: the gRPC servicer
returned an **empty** ``DiagnosisResponse`` on any exception (:161-166),
which Java then stored as a diagnosis with an empty label and
``rejected=false`` -- a fabricated result shown to a patient. The engine
raises instead, so the failure reaches the caller as
``50000``/``系统错误`` with no row written.

get.description:
``getOwnedDiagnosis`` (:282-290) + ``DiagnosisResultVO.objToVo``.

Ownership: a non-admin gets ``NO_AUTH_ERROR`` for someone else's row. Note
that ``NOT_FOUND_ERROR`` takes precedence over the ownership check, so the
existence of a row is disclosed before authorisation -- Java's order, kept
because the two codes drive different frontend flows.

post.description:
``DiagnosisServiceImpl.recordHumanReview`` (:255-279).

Only ``human*`` columns are writable. The AI conclusion is deliberately not
in :class:`DiagnosisResultDTO`, so no payload -- however crafted -- can
overwrite ``result``/``probability``/``details``/``aiRejected`` through this
route. That is a schema-level guarantee, not a field-by-field filter.

Validation order is copied because each branch has its own message:
not-admin -> ``仅管理员可写入人工复核字段``, blank ``humanResult`` ->
``必须填写人工结论``.
``listNewsVOByPage``. No ``@AuthCheck`` -- the news list is public.

post.summary: 获取分页新闻列表（缓存版）
post.description:
``listNewsVOByPageWithCache`` (:76-105).

The key is ``md5(json(dto))`` with **no user scoping** -- unlike the user
and diagnosis caches. That is correct here: the payload is public news, so
there is nothing to leak between users.

``json(dto)`` is not byte-identical to Hutool's, so an entry written by Java
is a miss rather than a misparse. Harmless, and only reachable before
Nginx finishes the cutover.

get.description:
``getNewsVO`` (:106-114).

The controller builds the VO *before* the null check, which is safe only
because ``getNewsVO(null)`` returns null (``NewsServiceImpl.java:84-86``).
Checked first here.

post.description:
**Physical** delete.

``News.java`` carries no ``@TableLogic`` annotation and ``t_news`` has no
``isDelete`` column, so MyBatis Plus issues ``DELETE FROM t_news`` and the
row is gone -- including any ``t_paragraph``/``t_attachment`` rows that
reference it, since those declare no foreign key constraint in
``schema.sql:71-77``. That is the existing behaviour and is reproduced as-is.

Returns ``false`` for a row that is already gone, as Java does.

Inline article images.

Returns a bare URL string, not an object -- the frontend collects the
result into an array of ``src`` values (``NewsEditPage.vue:91-100``).
Nothing is written to ``t_news``; ``t_attachment`` is untouched by this
endpoint despite the table existing.

``updateNews`` (:146-164).

``saveOrUpdate`` with a non-null id resolves to ``updateById``, which under
MyBatis Plus's default ``NOT_NULL`` field strategy writes **only the fields
the DTO populated**. Absent fields are left alone rather than nulled. This
port builds the UPDATE from the fields actually supplied, which is the
same rule.

``editTime`` is deliberately **not** touched. The DTO has no such field and
the DDL's ``DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`` applies to INSERT only (there is no
``ON UPDATE`` clause), so in Java a news row's edit time reflects the last
cover upload, not the last edit.

Two consequences of the faithful port, both existing Java behaviour:

* Re-saving an article with no actual change reports ``操作失败``.
  ``updateById`` returns the affected-row count, and MySQL counts *changed*
  rows by default, so a no-op UPDATE is 0. The frontend shows "保存失败"
  for an article that was, in fact, saved correctly.
* ``id`` must already exist. A new id means ``UPDATE`` matches nothing and
  the same ``操作失败`` is returned -- this endpoint cannot create an
  article.

``NewsServiceImpl.uploadCoverImage`` (:104-139).

This endpoint carries the most surprising behaviour in the domain, and the
frontend depends on all of it:

* **Without an ``id`` it cannot succeed.** It inserts a ``News`` populated
  only with ``title``/``userId``/``coverImg``, but ``content`` and
  ``publishTime`` are ``NOT NULL`` with no default
  (``schema.sql:57,61``). The INSERT always fails and the catch-all reports
  ``50000``/``系统错误``.
* **With an ``id`` it overwrites two unrelated columns.** ``title`` is set
  to ``""`` and ``userId`` to the *uploader's* id before the UPDATE, and
  MyBatis Plus writes empty strings (only nulls are skipped). So uploading a
  cover wipes the article's title and reassigns its author.

  The admin editor is built around this: ``NewsEditPage.vue`` uploads the
  cover first, then POSTs ``/edit`` with the real title, restoring it. A
  user who uploads a cover and then closes the tab leaves the article with
  an empty title and a changed author.

  Both columns are written here for fidelity. Dropping them would be
  invisible to the two-step flow and strictly safer, but it is a behaviour
  change rather than a port -- see ruling 21 for the recommendation.
* Returns the cover URL as a bare string, like ``/uploadAttachment``.

post.description:
``KnowledgeBaseServiceImpl.uploadDocument``.

Multipart field is ``files`` -- **plural**, unlike every other upload in the
project, which uses ``file``. Binding ``file`` here would silently accept
nothing.

Returns the ids that were stored. Per-file failures are in ``msg``; the
``data`` list remains compatible with the frontend client.

post.summary: 分页查询我的知识库文档
post.description:
``listPage``.

Newest first, scoped to the caller. Returns the raw entity -- there is no
VO in Java, so ``contentHash``, ``fileUrl`` and ``isDelete`` are all on the
wire. Reproduced rather than desensitized: the frontend's generated client
declares those fields.

delete.description:
``deleteDocument``.

**DELETE with a request body.** ``@DeleteMapping`` + ``@RequestBody
DeleteRequest`` -- unusual, and some proxies drop bodies on DELETE. Nginx is
configured to pass them through (Phase 3); if that fails, the query-parameter
fallback would need a matching frontend change (finding R5).

Cleanup order is vectors -> COS -> row, and each step catches its own
failure so a Chroma outage still removes the database row. The consequence
is real and reproduced: orphaned vectors stay in the collection, invisible
and unreachable, since they can only be deleted by id and no id survives the
row.

Always returns ``true``. The failures are logged, never surfaced.

post.description:
``McpServerServiceImpl.createMcp``.

Returns the generated ``mcpServerCode`` as a string.

The policy check runs before the insert, so a rejected config leaves no
row -- ``assertUserConfigAllowed`` is at :44, ``insert`` at :51.

put.description:
``McpServerServiceImpl.updateMcp``.

``status`` is **not** touched: an update cannot resurrect a deleted server,
because the lookup already excludes ``status = 3``.

get.summary: 分页查询 MCP 服务器
get.description:
``McpServerServiceImpl.listMcpServers``.

The page-size parameter is ``size``, not ``pageSize`` -- every other domain
in this project uses ``pageSize``. Getting it wrong is a silent 400 on every
call from a client that shares a helper with the other domains.

Soft-deleted servers are excluded, newest first.

delete.description:
``McpServerServiceImpl.deleteMcp`` -- a **soft** delete via ``status=3``.

No ``isDelete`` column exists on this table, so the row survives; every
query filters ``ne(status, 3)`` and the Agent filters ``status = 1``.

The path placeholder is camelCase to match Java's
``@DeleteMapping("/{mcpServerCode}")``. Placeholder names are not part of a
URL, so this is cosmetic -- but ``npm run openapi`` regenerates the TS
client from this spec, and a snake_case placeholder would rename the
generated ``deleteMcpServer`` parameter for no benefit.

get.summary: 获取 MCP 服务器详情
get.description:
``McpServerServiceImpl.getMcp``.

``needTools=true`` is the one branch Python cannot serve: it asks
``MCPManager`` to open a connection to the remote server and enumerate its
tools. That is MCP client code, and the MCP client is Agent subsystem --
which stays on Java by the migration's terms.

Rather than reimplementing an MCP client in Python (duplicating Agent
functionality, for stdio/SSE/Streamable-HTTP) or returning an empty list
that reads as "this server has no tools", it fails loudly. No frontend code
reaches this: ``frontend/src/api/mcpController.ts`` exports
``getMcpServer`` and nothing imports it.

If a caller ever needs it, the fix belongs in Java -- expose tool listing as
its own endpoint that this router can proxy to, rather than moving the MCP
client.

One authoritative snapshot per GET; done ends transport, not the task.

Clients renew this bounded stream, including after terminal workflow states:
consent and supplementary interactions can still change. Each renewal checks
Java identity and ownership; no transaction or identity cache spans renewals.

DeleteRequest.title: DeleteRequest
DeleteRequest.description:
``common/DeleteRequest.java`` -- one ``Long``.

Sent as the **body of a DELETE**. ``@DeleteMapping`` + ``@RequestBody`` is
legal in Spring but some proxies drop DELETE bodies; the Nginx config in
Phase 3 must forward them.

DiagnosisManageVO.title: DiagnosisManageVO
DiagnosisManageVO.description:
``model/vo/diagnosis/DiagnosisManageVO.java`` -- 11 fields.

Built from ``objToVo`` plus ``getDiagnosisManageVO``, which enriches each
row with the owner's ``userName`` via
``selectUserNameAndUserAvatarByUserId``.

``status`` is not a column: ``DiagnosisManageVO.java:66`` initialises it to
``COMPLETED`` at field-declaration time, so every row reports "已完成"
regardless of ``reexamineStatus``.

DiagnosisQueryDTO.title: DiagnosisQueryDTO
DiagnosisQueryDTO.description:
``DiagnosisQueryDTO.java`` -- ``extends common/PageRequest.java``.

``current``/``pageSize``/``sortOrder`` defaults are reproduced because a
request body may omit them and Java still applies them server-side.

``userId`` is accepted but **always overwritten** by the controller with the
session user's id before the query runs. It is kept so that a client posting
someone else's id is silently ignored rather than 400ing.

DiagnosisResultDTO.title: DiagnosisResultDTO
DiagnosisResultDTO.description:
``DiagnosisResultDTO.java`` -- human review write, admin only.

Deliberately contains no AI fields. ``recordHumanReview`` copies only
``human*`` onto the row, so a client cannot overwrite ``result``/
``probability``/``details``/``aiRejected`` through this endpoint.

DiagnosisResultVO.title: DiagnosisResultVO
DiagnosisResultVO.description:
``model/vo/diagnosis/DiagnosisResultVO.java`` -- 26 fields.

This is the payload the patient-facing result page renders, so every field
here is user-visible. ``disclaimer`` is declared because the frontend reads
it, but Java never sets it -- it is always ``null``, and the disclaimer text
the UI shows is hardcoded in the Vue component.

Disease.title: Disease
Disease.description:
``model/vo/diagnosis/Disease.java`` -- 2 fields.

``name`` is the **English** model label (``normal``, ``amd``, ...) because
it comes straight from the proto's ``top_predictions``. The Chinese label
the patient sees is ``DiagnosisResultVO.result``, not this.

KnowledgePageQuery.title: KnowledgePageQuery
KnowledgePageQuery.description:
``common/PageRequest.java``.

Only ``current`` and ``pageSize`` are read by ``listPage`` -- the
``sortField``/``sortOrder`` it inherits are ignored, because the query is
hardcoded to ``orderByDesc(createTime)``. Declared anyway so a body
carrying them is accepted rather than rejected.

LoginUserVO.title: LoginUserVO
LoginUserVO.description:
``model/vo/user/LoginUserVO.java``.

All 11 fields are declared because the frontend reads them directly. The
last three are vestigial: ``gender``/``phone``/``email`` are commented out
in ``User.java`` and the VO fills them with a constant 0 and two nulls.
They are kept so the payload is byte-identical.

Named to match the Java VO rather than the entity on purpose: the OpenAPI
schema name lands in the generated TypeScript as ``API.LoginUserVO``, and
``stores/user.ts``, ``checkAccess.ts`` and the header components all type
against that name.

Field types are declared, not inferred from the ORM, and the projection is
by keyword (:func:`login_user_vo`) so ``user_password`` cannot leak into a
response even by accident.

McpServerDetail.title: McpServerDetail
McpServerDetail.description:
``model/dto/mcp/McpServerDetail.java`` -- 8 fields.

Also the request body for create (``POST``) and update (``PUT``), which is
why every field except the handle is optional: Java's
``validateCreateParams`` enforces the real constraints and reads
``deployConfig`` first, before ``name``.

NewsQueryDTO.title: NewsQueryDTO
NewsQueryDTO.description:
``NewsQueryDTO.java`` -- ``extends common/PageRequest.java``.

``userRole`` is accepted and ignored: ``getNewsQueryWrapper`` never reads it.

NewsUpdateDTO.title: NewsUpdateDTO
NewsUpdateDTO.description:
``NewsUpdateDTO.java``.

``coverImage`` is declared but **deliberately not written**.

``BeanUtils.copyProperties(newsUpdateDTO, news)`` matches properties by
name; the DTO says ``coverImage`` and the entity says ``coverImg``, so the
copy silently drops it. The frontend sends the field on every save
(``NewsEditPage.vue:109``) and nothing ever complains -- it works only
because the cover was already persisted by ``POST /news/uploadCover`` in a
separate step. Reproduced as-is: honouring it here would be a behaviour
change, not a port. See ruling 21.

NewsUploadDTO.title: NewsUploadDTO
NewsUploadDTO.description:
``NewsUploadDTO.java`` -- one ``id``, used by ``/uploadCover`` to decide
between insert and update.

NewsVO.title: NewsVO
NewsVO.description:
``model/vo/news/NewsVO.java`` -- 8 fields.

``author``/``avatar`` are enriched from ``t_user`` on every read.
``coverImage`` comes from the ``coverImg`` column. ``status`` is
deliberately absent -- ``NewsVO`` does not declare it, so the frontend
cannot tell a draft from a published article.

UserAddDTO.title: UserAddDTO
UserAddDTO.description:
``UserAddDTO.java`` -- admin-created user.

``userPassword`` is required by ``UserController.java:115-118`` even though
the Java field itself is nullable.

UserEditDTO.title: UserEditDTO
UserEditDTO.description:
``UserEditDTO.java`` -- self-service profile edit.

Deliberately has no ``id``: ``UserServiceImpl#updateOwnProfile`` always
writes to the session user's id and ignores any client-supplied one.

UserLoginDTO.title: UserLoginDTO
UserLoginDTO.description:
``model/dto/user/UserLoginDTO.java``.

``extra="ignore"`` so a login body that happens to carry extra keys still
authenticates, matching Java's bean binding.

UserQueryDTO.title: UserQueryDTO
UserQueryDTO.description:
``UserQueryDTO.java`` -- ``extends common/PageRequest.java``.

The Java DTO extends ``PageRequest``, so it inherits ``current`` (1),
``pageSize`` (10), ``sortField`` and ``sortOrder`` ("descend"). Those
defaults are reproduced here because a request body omitting them still
gets them server-side in Java -- the frontend relies on that when posting
``{userName: "x"}`` and nothing else.

UserVO.title: UserVO
UserVO.description:
``model/vo/user/UserVO.java`` -- the desensitized view (7 fields).

No ``userPassword``, no ``isDelete``.
